answer: The bond is locked for 34 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. Because the crystal lockup is enforced by the grove escrow, the tide audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. Running a large fleet as a result freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants pay once per identity. That is 28 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
